## assertResponse() (assert-response)

Parse and assert one expected response type, throwing on an error or a mismatch.

The strict alternative to parseResponse + manual narrowing: it parses, rethrows a CLIError as an Error carrying the CLI message, and rejects any envelope whose `type` is not the one you asked for. Use it when a call site expects exactly one response type and any other outcome is a bug worth failing on.

Import it from `@astryxdesign/cli/json`.

`raw` (required) = `unknown` = The CLI stdout to parse: a JSON string, or an object that was already parsed.
`expectedType` (required) = `string` = The response discriminant the caller requires (e.g. 'component.detail').

`any` = The parsed envelope, guaranteed at runtime to carry the requested `type`. The published signature is untyped; cast to the matching *Response type for typed access.

`Error` = a plain Error with no code: the CLI returned an error envelope (its message is rethrown; code and suggestions are dropped), or the response `type` is not expectedType

## blog() (blog)

List blog posts, or read one, from the published RSS feed.

Reads the design system blog the same way any feed reader does, over the published RSS feed, never the blog's source files. With no slug it lists every post parsed from the feed; with a slug it reads that post's full plaintext body via the .txt alternate the feed advertises. Both envelopes carry feedUrl so a caller can hit the RSS feed directly.

Import it from `@astryxdesign/cli/api`.

`slug` = `string` = Post slug (matched case-insensitively) to read in full. Omit to list every post.

`blog.list` = The feed URL plus every post parsed from the feed, each with slug, title, description, date, type, authors, link, and its plaintext URL.
`blog.detail` = One post's metadata plus the feed URL and the post's full plaintext body.

`ERR_INVALID_ARGUMENT` = the slug is provided but is not a string
`ERR_UNKNOWN_POST` = no post in the feed matches the requested slug
`ERR_FETCH_FAILED` = the RSS feed or post text cannot be fetched (network error, timeout, non-2xx, or oversized), or the post has no plaintext alternate in the feed

`npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 blog` runs it. Read it with `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs cli/commands/blog`.

## build() (build)

Page-building assistant: the how-to-build playbook, or the page template to start from for an idea.

The "build a page" entry point. Called with no query it returns the how-to-build-a-page playbook as data: the workflow steps with their commands, the on-system rules, and related lookups. Called with a query it names the page template to START from (always one: the page template a ranker built for long descriptions puts first; for a part of a page, the page it names; else the app shell) and the next two templates, and the unified search grouped around it: the other close page templates, drop-in blocks, and idea-specific components/hooks, plus the always-on frame + foundation. A template carries the page frame and spacing, so the kit never recommends composing a page from components.

Import it from `@astryxdesign/cli/api`.

`query` = `string` = What you're building (e.g. "analytics dashboard"). Omit for the how-to-build playbook.
`options.cwd` = `string` = process.cwd() = Directory to resolve @astryxdesign/core and templates from.
`options.type` = `'component' | 'hook' | 'doc' | 'template' | 'theme'` = Restrict the underlying search to a single domain.
`options.limit` = `number` = 60 = Max results pulled from search before grouping into the kit.

`build.help` = Emitted when the query is omitted: the page-building playbook — `playbook: true`, a `title`, the ordered `steps` (each a `title`, its `commands`, and optionally what the step `returns`), the on-system `rules`, and `related` lookups. Each command is a bare subcommand ({command, purpose?}) for the caller to render with its own CLI invocation.
`build.kit` = The page template to start from and the kit around it: the echoed query, hasResults/matchCount/directMatch fields, `start` (the template to scaffold, the `template <id> --type page <path>` command that selects it, whether the page ranker's pick is also search's direct match, the closest page, or the fallback app shell, the ranker's next two `alternatives`, and optional `notes` — setup notes naming what the template needs that the project lacks, such as missing packages or a missing StyleX compiler), search's closest page templates (≤3), drop-in block patterns (≤5), idea-specific components/hooks (≤6), and the always-on frame + foundation component-name arrays. Carries `hint` only when the kit came back thin — what to try instead, so a caller does not read a near-empty kit as "the package has nothing".

`ERR_INVALID_ARGUMENT` = a query is given and options.type is not a known domain, or options.limit is not a positive integer
`ERR_CORE_NOT_FOUND` = a query is given and @astryxdesign/core cannot be found from cwd
`ERR_VERSIONS_UNAVAILABLE` = a query is given outside a project, or in a project with nothing installed, and the Core of the release that answers is not beside it or cached, and cannot be installed into the per-user cache (offline, a registry without it, or an unwritable cache)

`npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 build` runs it. Read it with `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs cli/commands/build`.

## component() (component)

Resolve one or several components by name, or list the catalog, with optional focused slices (props, source, showcase, blocks).

Routes on its arguments: one string resolves that component across core and integration packages; an array returns one ordered result row per selector at every array length; and no name returns the catalog grouped by category. Boolean flags narrow each resolved component to just its props, source, showcase, or example blocks. An integration component that replaces a Core component (its doc sets replaces, and its package declares the CLI range that turns replacement on) answers to the Core name in detail, batch, and list results; use options.package '@astryxdesign/core' for the original. In global mode: with `cwd` outside a project, components from integrations installed next to this CLI package globally resolve too; inside a project, only the project's own integrations count. See `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs global` and `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs global/computer-integrations`.

Import it from `@astryxdesign/cli/api`.

`name` = `string | string[]` = Pass one selector string for the existing single-result response, or an array of at most 100 selectors for an ordered component.batch response. The limit counts duplicates in every projection mode. An array always requests a batch, including [] and ['Button']. Use 'Button', 'widgets/Button', '@acme/widgets/Button', or '@acme/widgets@1.2.3/Button'. A version applies to the package and must match the installed version. Omit the argument to list the catalog.
`options.cwd` = `string` = process.cwd() = Directory to resolve @astryxdesign/core from.
`options.list` = `boolean` = Return the grouped catalog instead of a single component.
`options.category` = `string` = List only the components in this group: a key of the unfiltered list (each component's group field), such as 'Layout' or 'Button'. It is not the category field of a component detail.
`options.package` = `string` = Scope lookup to a specific external package (e.g. '@acme/widgets'). Use '@astryxdesign/core' to select an original replaced by an integration component.
`options.props` = `boolean` = Return only the component's props table.
`options.source` = `boolean` = Return the component's source file.
`options.showcase` = `boolean` = Return the component's showcase example.
`options.blocks` = `boolean` = Return the component's example blocks (showcase, examples, related).
`options.detail` = `'full' | 'compact' | 'brief'` = 'full' for a named component; 'brief' for lists (returned as data.detail: 'names') = Detail level for list views.
`options.lang` = `string` = Language code for localized doc content: 'en', 'zh', or 'dense'.
`options.zh` = `boolean` = Shorthand for Chinese (zh) doc content.
`options.dense` = `boolean` = Return the token-efficient dense doc variant.

`component.list` = The catalog grouped by component group. data.detail is the level ('names' | 'compact' | 'full') and data.components is the grouped map: names entries with name, package, and an optional canonical import for integration and legacy package components; brief entries; or full ComponentDoc entries.
`component.batch` = An explicit selector array returns one ordered receipt at every array length: count and one results row per selector, including duplicates. ComponentBatchResponse specializes the shared BatchResponse and BatchRow types. Each row carries selector and status (found, not_found, ambiguous, or error); found rows carry the single-selector result, ambiguous rows carry installed candidates ({package, component, kind, installed}), and failed rows carry code, error, and optional suggestions.
`component.detail` = One component's authored ComponentDoc plus ownership metadata (owner package, import specifier, whether source is available). When the name is a sub-component documented in a parent's doc, the payload is scoped to it and parentDoc names that parent.
`component.detail.props` = Just the component's props table (ComponentPropDoc[]).
`component.detail.source` = The component's source file, as {component, source}.
`component.detail.showcase` = The component's showcase example, as {component, aspectRatio, source}.
`component.detail.blocks` = The component's example blocks, as {component, showcase, examples, related} of BlockEntry.

`ERR_INVALID_ARGUMENT` = a selector array has more than 100 entries, a package-shaped selector has no component item, or its package conflicts with options.package
`ERR_INVALID_DETAIL` = options.detail is not 'full', 'compact', or 'brief'
`ERR_INVALID_LANG` = options.lang is set to anything other than 'en', 'zh', or 'dense'
`ERR_CORE_NOT_FOUND` = @astryxdesign/core cannot be resolved from cwd
`ERR_VERSIONS_UNAVAILABLE` = outside a project, or in a project with nothing installed, the Core of the release that answers is not beside it or cached, and cannot be installed into the per-user cache (offline, a registry without it, or an unwritable cache)
`ERR_UNKNOWN_CATEGORY` = options.category is not a string or matches no component group
`ERR_UNKNOWN_COMPONENT` = name is not a string, resolves to no known component, or is absent from the requested options.package
`ERR_AMBIGUOUS_COMPONENT` = the component is provided by multiple packages (pass options.package to disambiguate)
`ERR_UNKNOWN_PACKAGE` = options.package names a legacy external package that cannot be found, or a package-qualified selector requests a version that is not installed
`ERR_NO_DOC` = the resolved component has no .doc.mjs typed doc file
`ERR_INVALID_DOC` = the resolved component's .doc.mjs fails to load or validate
`ERR_NO_SOURCE` = options.source is set but the component has no source file
`ERR_NO_SHOWCASE` = options.showcase is set but the component has no showcase

## discover() (discover)

Browse and search integrations: the ones a project has and, through the official list and discover sources, the ones it could add.

Lists the integrations a project loads and the official packages it declares, then the packages it could add: the official Astryx packages first, from the list the CLI carries, then whatever the discover sources of the project and its integrations list, with what each one adds per kind. An @scope/name query shows one package with every version its source knows; @scope/name@version shows one version; @scope/name/Component returns an installed component's validated doc, and any other item path returns that item. A free-text term searches every item and package. Discover only reads: it prints the command that adds a package and never runs it. In global mode: with `cwd` outside a project, integrations installed next to this CLI package globally are listed as installed; inside a project, only the project's own are, and the compatible global ones are listed in `meta.available` with source `installed for this computer` and an `install` command. See `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs global` and `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs global/computer-integrations`.

Import it from `@astryxdesign/cli/api`.

`query` = `string` = A package (@scope/name, optionally @version), an item path (@scope/name/<item>), or a free-text term. Omit to list packages.
`options.components` = `boolean` = In the CLI package list, print every component, and every other item, of each package instead of the first 10. A display flag for the CLI renderer; the programmatic response is unchanged.
`options.type` = `'component' | 'template' | 'doc' | 'theme' | 'codemod' | 'agent-doc'` = Only one kind: in the list, packages that add it; in a search, items of that kind.
`options.installed` = `boolean` = false = Only what the project has. Cannot be set with options.available.
`options.available` = `boolean` = false = Only what the project could add. Cannot be set with options.installed.
`options.limit` = `number` = 20 = Max number of search results, a positive integer.
`options.lang` = `string` = Language code to translate a resolved component doc into.
`options.zh` = `boolean` = false = Return a resolved component doc in Chinese.

`discover.list` = What the project has: the integrations it loads and the official packages it declares (package, the npm package and always equal to name; name, category, components, version, and a list per other kind they add), official packages first. meta.available lists what the project could add, official packages first, each with its package and the command that adds it; inside a project, an integration installed for the computer that the project does not install is listed there too, with source `installed for this computer` and the install command for the project in `install`. meta.sources reports each source, the official list last. When it lists no integration it carries meta.configured.
`discover.detail` = One package: its package (the npm package the result is about), what the shown version adds, whether the project has it, its versions and latest release when a source knows them, and the command that adds it when the project does not have it. An entry from the official list lists the newest release this CLI knows as latest and the project's Core version; its add command pins the project's Core version, else the Core range it declares (quoted), else the latest release. A version or item the official list does not show answers ERR_UNKNOWN_PACKAGE.
`discover.detail.doc` = The validated ComponentDoc for one installed component, for an @scope/name/Component query, plus package, the npm package that owns the component.
`discover.item` = One item that is not an installed component: its kind, name, the package and version that add it, and whether the project has the package. The envelope's package names the same package.
`discover.search` = The query echoed back plus every matching item and package, each with its kind and whether the project has it, even when one name matches exactly or only one item matches; total is set when the limit cut the list.

`ERR_INVALID_ARGUMENT` = the query is a non-string value, or a free-text search is run with an empty query
`ERR_INVALID_OPTION` = options.type is not a known kind, options.limit is not a positive integer, or options.installed and options.available are both set
`ERR_UNKNOWN_PACKAGE` = neither the project, the official list, nor any discover source has the package
`ERR_UNKNOWN_COMPONENT` = the item is not in the named package
`ERR_NOT_FOUND` = a free-text term matches nothing, or the requested version is not published
`ERR_INVALID_DOC` = the resolved component's docs fail to load or are malformed

`npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 discover` runs it. Read it with `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs cli/commands/discover`.

## docs() (docs)

Read the reference docs: list every topic, one topic's sections, one section, or a whole topic.

No topic lists every reference-doc topic; a topic returns its whole ReferenceDoc, and `index: true` returns its section index (each section's key, title, and summary); a topic plus a section returns that one section. Token-ref blocks are inlined in every read, and so is a section's reference block: the doc it includes, then the command that opens that doc. The topic set is the CLI's own docs plus the ones the project's configured integrations contribute, including any topic an integration replaces or extends, so it depends on the cwd. A route opens a node of the docs tree instead: a namespace such as `cli/api` returns its children one level down (`depth` reads as many levels as asked, and `detail` how much of each doc below), a typed doc such as `cli/api/functions/search` returns its content, and a guide the tree places (`authoring/quick-start`) reads like any topic. Every read but the list carries `links`, the commands that move from it: `up` to the level it sits in, `previous` and `next` to its neighbors, and, for a typed doc, `related` to the docs it names (its command or function, and its related docs); `previous` and `next` to the section or node before and after it. Overlay options select localized or dense variants. In global mode: with `cwd` outside a project, doc topics from integrations installed next to this CLI package globally are listed too; inside a project, only the project's own integrations count. See `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs global` and `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs global/computer-integrations`.

Import it from `@astryxdesign/cli/api`.

`topic` = `string` = Doc topic to load (e.g. 'principles'), a docs-tree route (e.g. 'cli/api/functions/search'), or the name of one node of the docs tree: its own name (e.g. 'tokens-color'), or its route without the prefix its name repeats (e.g. 'tokens/color'), where exactly one node answers to it. Omit to list all topics.
`section` = `string` = Section to return: its key (from the topic's index), its title, or a unique part of its title (case-insensitive).
`options.lang` = `string` = Language code for localized doc content.
`options.zh` = `boolean` = Shorthand for Chinese (zh) doc content.
`options.dense` = `boolean` = Return the token-efficient dense doc variant. It is written to be read whole, so it returns the whole doc.
`options.index` = `boolean` = Return the topic's section index (each section's key, title, and summary), even for a topic with one section.
`options.depth` = `number | 'all'` = How many levels below a docs-tree namespace to read: 0 for the namespace alone, 1 for its children (the default), 'all' for every level. Where a read stops, a child with docs below it carries childCount. A doc with nothing below it reads the same at any depth. On the topic list, where each namespace otherwise lists alone, it names the docs below each one, as deep as asked; without it the list is unchanged.
`options.detail` = `'brief' | 'compact' | 'full'` = How much of each doc below the named one a depth read returns: brief (the default) is its identity; compact and full add its text (a guide's sections, a namespace's or typed doc's content). Given alone, it reads one level down. The topic list names each doc below a namespace by its identity whatever the detail.
`options.cwd` = `string` = Project directory whose configured integrations contribute topics. Defaults to process.cwd(); an unreadable config falls back to the CLI's own topics.

`docs.list` = Every reference-doc topic in read order, as DocsListEntry[] ({topic, description, package, replaces?, replacedPackage?}), each readable with docs(topic). meta.namespaces lists the docs tree's top-level namespaces ({topic, description, package}); with depth, each also carries children, the docs below it as a namespace read names them ({topic, description, route, name, package, kind, title, summary, replaces?, replacedPackage?, stability?}), nested the same way to the depth asked for, and childCount where the depth stops on a doc with docs below it. meta.notLoaded names each package whose docs did not load ({package, message}).
`docs.detail` = One topic's full ReferenceDoc, with token-ref and reference blocks inlined, plus links.
`docs.index` = One topic's section index (index: true): {name, title, description, sections: [{id, title, summary}], links}.
`docs.detail.section` = One ReferenceSection of the topic, found by key or title, with token-ref and reference blocks inlined. Asked of a docs-tree namespace, it is the section read of the one guide below the namespace that has the section.
`docs.node` = A namespace or typed doc in the docs tree, read by its route: {id, route, kind, package, title, summary, breadcrumb, slots, content}. A namespace lists each slot's children one level down, or as deep as depth asks, each child carrying its own slots, childCount where the read stops, and its text at compact or full detail; a typed doc carries its content.

`ERR_INVALID_ARGUMENT` = depth is not a whole number of levels or 'all'
`ERR_INVALID_DETAIL` = detail is not brief, compact, or full
`ERR_UNKNOWN_TOPIC` = the topic is not a string, or matches no topic, no docs-tree route, and no one node of the docs tree by its own name or by its route without the prefix its name repeats; a name more than one node answers to opens none of them, and the suggestions list them
`ERR_UNKNOWN_SECTION` = a section is requested but is empty, matches no section, or matches more than one; asked of a docs-tree namespace, when no guide below it or more than one has the section (suggestions name those guides); or asked of a typed doc, which has no sections

`npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs` runs it. Read it with `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs cli/commands/docs`.

## doctor() (doctor)

Check a project's Astryx setup and get a pass/warn/fail report per check. Use it as a CI gate or before debugging a broken install.

Runs a series of diagnostics: Node version, @astryxdesign/core install and version alignment with the CLI, installed themes and wiring, astryx.config validity, whether every integration astryx.config names loads (a failed one fails the run), integrations linked from package.json without a config entry, core peer dependencies, integration provider identity and contribution issues, agent docs, the detected package manager, and the health of the docs the CLI reads (authoring and CLI docs, the docs tree, doc size), and returns a structured report. Theme checks run when the generated app module exists; without one, doctor reports that the CLI manages no themes and names theme add, and the `themes` check counts a theme as wired when package.json `astryx.theme` names one or when the source of the app (JavaScript, TypeScript and CSS files, outside dependencies and build output; type-only imports do not count) imports the built module or stylesheet of a discovered theme, the same imports theme add writes, or passes one to Theme (followed through module-scope variables, defineTheme extends, re-exports and installed packages; only a theme whose package is installed, or a local theme, counts), naming the file; a theme passed to Theme that cannot be traced, such as a prop or a variable declared inside a component, is reported as unconfirmed (info), not as missing. Earlier descriptor-less copies are a non-failing upgrade warning. It never installs, writes, or mutates. It imports astryx.config, executes every added theme source while validating private inputs, and loads every recorded built theme module to prove its runtime imports work, including themes from installed packages. Local theme source also runs during build-freshness checks. Stylesheets are parsed without execution. Config and theme top-level code therefore run, so use doctor only with project code you trust. Outside a project it checks the computer instead: the Node version (`node-version`), the release that answered (`answering-release`), the newest release the computer knows of (`newest-release`), the astryx commands on the search path (`cli-on-path`), the integrations installed for the computer (`computer-integrations`: each one used outside a project, and a warning for one skipped because its peer range excludes the answering release or that fails to load), and the computer-level agent text (`computer-agent-text`): present and matching this release, present but different, edited, absent, or turned off, and where it is linked, with `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 init --user` as the fix for the stale and absent cases. The agent-text check is always info. The newest-release check also runs inside a project: it names a newer release when the computer knows of one; inside a project whose release is older it names the install and upgrade commands; outside one, when the CLI installed for the computer is older, it names the command of the package manager that installed it, after the Node the newest release needs when the computer runs an older one. It is always info and installs nothing. The `cli-on-path` check also runs inside a project: it lists every astryx command on the search path in order, passes when the first is a release that hands each project run to the release of that project, and warns when the first is another program or a release that predates the hand-off, naming `npm install -g @astryxdesign/cli@latest`. Inside a project, `computer-integrations` lists, as info, the integrations installed for the computer that the project does not install, with its install command; they are not used there. It never fails a check because the folder has no project, and installs nothing. In global mode: with `cwd` outside a project, it checks the computer instead (the Node version, the version that answered, the newest version it knows of, the astryx commands on the search path, the integrations installed globally, and the agent guide for the computer) and never fails a check because the folder has no project. See `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs global` and `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs global/who-answers`.

Import it from `@astryxdesign/cli/api`.

`options.cwd` = `string` = process.cwd() = Directory to diagnose. A directory outside any project, a missing one included, gets the computer checks.
`options.built` = `string` = A finished build to check before you deliver it: a project folder, a build output folder, or one built `.html` file, relative to `cwd`. Adds two checks after the others. `built-astryx-usage` fails when the path holds no value import from an Astryx package (any `@astryxdesign/*` package or an integration the project installs), no component imported from one, and no Astryx styles in built CSS or HTML. `built-astryx-purity` warns with the source check of `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs is-my-code-good`: raw elements Astryx has a component for, raw SVG and icon-library icons, inline styles, classes, `stylex.create` and imported stylesheets, each with its file and line, in `.tsx` and `.jsx` files and JSX in `.js` source, found by parsing it; it is info, not inspected, when the path holds no source with JSX, such as a bundle. It reads at most 20,000 files, each up to 5 MB, skipping installs and version control; when either limit leaves source unread and nothing was found, the purity check is info, not fully inspected, and when the file limit ends the read before any Astryx turns up, `built-astryx-usage` warns that the rest went unread instead of failing. Given one built `.html` file, it also reads the local stylesheets and scripts that page links, finding a root-relative link from the nearest folder above the page that holds it; a linked file that is not there makes `built-astryx-usage` warn instead of fail. An empty folder fails with nothing checked, like a missing path. A source tree counts as using Astryx through an import, a re-export (`export … from`) or a stylesheet `@import` of an Astryx package; a type-only import or re-export (`import type`, `export type`, or a list whose names are all `type`) does not count, since the build erases it. `--built` goes with `doctor` alone; a `doctor integration` check refuses it. A path that does not exist fails `built-astryx-usage` with nothing checked, and the purity check is left out. The integrations that count are the dependencies the nearest package.json above the path declares whose installed copy, found the way the CLI autolinks (a hoisted workspace copy included), has an integration manifest. The files under the path, and that configuration, are only read, never run. Without it, doctor runs exactly as before.

`doctor` = The diagnostic report: `data.checks`, each with a stable id, label, `status` (`pass` | `warn` | `fail` | `info`), a one-line message, and an optional `fix` (always present on `warn` and `fail`; some `info` checks carry one too); plus `data.summary` with counts per status.

`npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 doctor` runs it. Read it with `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs cli/commands/doctor`.

## exportSearchIndex() (export-search-index)

The candidates search ranks in a folder, as plain JSON to store and rank later with rankSearchIndex().

Gathers what `search()` would rank in `cwd` and returns it as `{version, candidates}`. Gathering reads each installed package's docs and loads its integration manifest, which runs that package's code, so a catalog that lists packages it must not load makes the index where loading is safe (a folder with those packages installed), stores it, and ranks it with `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs cli/api/functions/rank-search-index`. With `package`, the index keeps only that package's candidates, for a catalog that stores one index per package. A component description's inline doc tokens are resolved where the index is made, as `search` prints them; when Core could not be had there, the index says why in `coreSkipped`. Fields that point into the folder are left out, so an index reads the same wherever it was made. The candidates are the ranker's input, not a stable shape: an index is ranked only by the CLI version that made it. Experimental: it may change or be removed in a patch release.

Import it from `@astryxdesign/cli/api`.

`options.cwd` = `string` = process.cwd() = The folder to gather from, read as `search()` reads it.
`options.package` = `string` = Keep only the candidates this npm package owns: its components, templates, themes, and doc parts. Without it the index holds everything the folder's search ranks, Core's entries and the CLI's docs included.

`SearchIndex` = `version`, the CLI version that made it, and `candidates`, the gathered entries as plain JSON.

`ERR_INVALID_ARGUMENT` = `package` is given and is not a non-empty string

## gapReport() (gap-report)

Report a missing or hard-to-use design-system capability to the package that owns it.

Routes the report to the package that owns the gap: options.package when given, else the integration whose component replaces the named Core component, else the one package that provides the component, else Core. Sends a gap report to every configured handler: the project config handler first, then each integration handler in config order. Each handler has 30 s to finish, and its output goes to stderr. Public handlers run only with confirmPublic; internal handlers always run. ## integrationCheck() (integration-check)

Runs `validateIntegration`, `integrationComponentConflicts`, `integrationTemplateConflicts`, and `integrationDocConflicts` against the integration package in `options.cwd`, and counts each result the way that check's own subcommand exits. The run fails when any of the four would fail on its own. With `strict` it also fails on any warning and on any check that did not run: a package with no integration manifest, or a comparison a check carries that was skipped, such as one that needs the project's TypeScript. `strict` adds no check: it reports those warnings and skipped work again, as errors in the checks' own issue format. A new check, or a new failure code, joins only in a minor release, named in the release notes.

`options.next` = `boolean` = false = Also count the findings the next minor release turns into warnings, validate's notes marked `next`, as warnings now, so `strict` fails on them.

The totals are `data.errors`, `data.warnings`, and `data.skipped` (each reason prefixed with its check); an issue every check starts from, such as one about the manifest, counts once, and every other finding counts on its own. `data.unchecked` counts the items the checks list as not compared, which never fail it. `data.upcoming` counts the findings the next minor release turns into warnings (validate's notes marked `next`), and `data.next` says whether this run counted them as warnings now. ## integrationComponentConflicts() (integration-component-conflicts)

Check integration component names, replaces declarations, and documented props.

Loads one local or installed integration, compares its component names with Core, and returns non-blocking conflicts with the exact package-qualified component command required to keep an intentional overlap. Each component's replaces is checked too: its findings are issues, errors for a package that declares the CLI range that turns replacement on and warnings otherwise. A `{@link}` in a component doc's text that names no doc is an `invalid_doc_graph` warning, since it prints as written. Each component doc's props are compared with the component's TypeScript props, read with the project's own `typescript` (or, where `typescript` is missing or has no JavaScript compiler API, as TypeScript 7 does, the `@typescript/typescript6` it installs): a documented prop the code lacks, a prop the package declares that the doc omits, a wrong `required`, or a type that does not match. A type is judged only when it reads exactly: the same text as the source, once whitespace, quotes and union order are set aside (exactly, if it contains `readonly`), or primitives, literals, arrays and unions of those, or a name for one, on both sides, a field such as `status.type` included, and for a union of props types, the type of any one member. A field the prop's variants give different types is listed when the doc gives only some variants' types. A mutable array type matches a readonly one, because callers can pass it; a readonly one documented for a mutable array is a mismatch. `Name = …` with a union after it must match in both parts; one value after it (`Size = 'md'`) is read as a default. A name only TypeScript's own libraries declare is not resolved, and `React.X` resolves through React where the prop is declared. Every other type is listed as not compared, never reported, and so is a name an index signature takes unless exactly one the package declares takes it; with a TypeScript older than 4.8 no type is judged. Those findings are warnings in `propDrift`; without TypeScript it is `skipped` with a reason.

`pkg` = `string` = Installed package; omit for the local package.
`options.cwd` = `string` = Resolution directory.

`integration.component-conflicts` = `validated` (false when no integration manifest was found, so nothing was inspected), integration identity, structural and replaces issues, and Core component-name conflicts with package-qualified commands. An active replacement that keeps the Core name it replaces is not a conflict. When the manifest loads and declares a components root, `propDrift` holds the props comparison: `status` (`checked` | `skipped`), `reason` when skipped, `typescript`, `components` compared, `typesCompared` (documented prop types judged), `typesSkipped` (why none was, with a TypeScript older than 4.8), `findings` ({component, prop, kind: `not_in_code` | `not_in_doc` | `required_mismatch` | `type_mismatch` | `default_mismatch`, severity: `warning`, message, doc, source, docType?, codeType?, docRequired?, codeRequired?, docDefault?, codeDefault?, fix?}), `unchecked` ({component, doc, reason}), `typesNotCompared` ({component, doc, reason, props}: every other documented prop type, grouped by why it was not judged: not a form the check judges exactly (a doc type that does not parse, or a prop a mapped type builds from keys the check cannot trace, included), a field the prop's variants give different types, a standard prop such as `className`, or a prop declared outside the package), and `propsNotChecked` when a mapped type builds props from keys the check cannot trace to the package ({component, doc, reason, props}: no warning is drawn for those props).

## search() (search)

Unified ranked search across components, hooks, docs, templates, and themes.

The single "I'm looking for X" entry point across every content domain. Matching and scores are keyword + fuzzy (not embeddings). Between score bands results keep the lexical order, whose domain priority can put a weaker component, hook, template, or theme above a stronger doc, and a query that is an entry's exact name answers with that entry first. Inside a band, fixed weights order the matches, so a description match can lead a keyword match in the same band (55–99 holds both). A component's usage guidance (its best practices) is indexed one tier below its description, so the words a reader types still find it. In global mode: with `cwd` outside a project, items from integrations installed next to this CLI package globally are searched too, and theme results name no step that adds a theme to an app; inside a project, only the project's own integrations count. See `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs global` and `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs global/computer-integrations`.

Import it from `@astryxdesign/cli/api`.

`query` (required) = `string` = Free-text search term.
`options.type` = `'component' | 'hook' | 'doc' | 'template' | 'theme'` = Restrict results to a single domain.
`options.limit` = `number` = 20 = Maximum number of results.
`options.cwd` = `string` = Directory to resolve @astryxdesign/core from: the project's installed Core, else, outside a project or in a project with nothing installed, the Core of the release that answers, installed into the per-user cache first when needed. A docs-only or themes-only search (`type: 'doc'` or `type: 'theme'`) does not need it. A search with no `type` covers the docs and themes alone only when that Core cannot be obtained, and then says so in `meta.partial`.

`search` = The query echoed back, `matchCount` (how many candidates matched in total, before `limit`), plus a ranked SearchResultEntry[] bounded by `limit`: each has domain, name, score, reason, description, and follow-up command, plus `import` for components and hooks, `title` for docs, `displayName` and `kind` for templates, and `displayName` for themes. A deprecated component's result also carries `deprecated`, `{replacement, description}` from its doc: the name of the component to use instead and the modernization route. A doc result is the smallest part that answers: one section (with `section`, and a command that reads only it), one docs-tree route, or a topic, whose command lists its sections. `parent` is the command that opens the level above it: the section list of its topic, the namespace a tree node sits in, the topic level (Guides or Foundations) for a flat topic, or the topic list for a top-level namespace. Every doc result also carries `package`, the npm package that authored it (for a section, the package its file came from). A theme result is one theme you can import: `name` is its slug, its command is `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 theme add <slug>` (outside a project, where there is no app to add it to, `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 theme eject <slug>`), and `package` is the npm package that ships it (`@astryxdesign/cli` for the CLI's own themes). When a search with no `type` could not obtain @astryxdesign/core, `meta.partial` is `{skipped, reason}`: the domains it skipped (`component`, `hook`, `template`) and why; the results are the docs and themes, and text mode prints one line on standard error.

`ERR_INVALID_ARGUMENT` = the query is empty, --type is unknown, or --limit is not a positive integer
`ERR_CORE_NOT_FOUND` = @astryxdesign/core cannot be found from the cwd, and `type` names a domain that reads it: `component`, `hook`, or `template`
`ERR_VERSIONS_UNAVAILABLE` = `type` names a domain that reads @astryxdesign/core, and outside a project, or in a project with nothing installed, the Core of the release that answers cannot be installed into the per-user cache; a search with no `type` answers with `meta.partial` instead

`npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 search` runs it. Read it with `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs cli/commands/search`.

An output folder swizzle owns (one the copy creates, an empty one, or one it marked before) gets an astryx-swizzle.json marker naming each package its copies came from, with its version, so @astryxdesign/build's Babel, PostCSS and Vite integrations, and withAstryx() under webpack, compile the copy below the theme. The receipt flags whether any copied file uses StyleX and lists each npm package the copy imports with the range the owner package declares. With no name (or list) it returns the swizzlable component names instead. ## themeBuild() (theme-build)

Compile a defineTheme() file to scoped CSS, a JS module, and type declarations, or check committed outputs for drift in CI.

The compiler behind `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 theme build`. Reads a file that calls defineTheme() and writes a scoped CSS file, a JS module that re-exports the built theme, and a .d.ts (plus an optional .variants.d.ts when the theme adds custom prop values). It uses @astryxdesign/core's own generator, so the CSS matches what the <Theme> runtime emits. When another build step emits the icon registry, {iconsSpecifier} declares the fully specified module path for the generated JS import. Real registry imports are preserved, including aliases, default imports, and namespace imports. Icons inherited through extends are retained, with child entries taking precedence. Comment and string contents do not affect import detection. An inline registry that cannot be preserved fails with ERR_THEME_INVALID before any output is written, including in check mode. Move the registry to its own module and import it into the theme file. With {check: true} it writes nothing and instead compares each output against disk, returning the drift: the CI guard for committed, generated theme CSS.

Import it from `@astryxdesign/cli/api`.

`file` (required) = `string` = Path to a theme file that calls defineTheme(), resolved against cwd.
`options.out` = `string` = Override the output CSS path, relative or absolute; a build refuses a path outside cwd, and check mode refuses only a relative path that escapes cwd. The .js, .d.ts and any .variants.d.ts are written in the same directory, named after the theme (<name>.js), not after the CSS file.
`options.check` = `boolean` = false = Compile in memory and compare each output against what is on disk instead of writing: the CI drift guard. Because it writes nothing, it also compares outputs outside cwd; when those are stale, the report names the directory that contains them and the build and check commands to run from there, since a build refuses them and each output records the directory it was built from.
`options.iconsSpecifier` = `string` = Override the selected icon-registry import specifier in the generated JS module, for example ./icons.mjs. With child and inherited registries, this changes the child registry import. When omitted, direct source specifiers are preserved; relative imports followed through a local base are rebased to the theme file. A registry inherited through a package theme must be imported directly to use this option.
`ctx.cwd` = `string` = process.cwd() = Directory the theme file, a relative out path, and the returned output paths resolve against. Every output a build writes is inside it, including the default outputs beside the theme file.

`theme.build` = Build receipt {name, tokenCount, componentCount, sizeKB, outputs, warnings, notices}: the theme name; how many tokens (portable plus theme-local) and component targets it overrides; the CSS size in KB; the written outputs {css, cssDts for strict side-effect imports, js, dts, and variantsDts when custom prop values were augmented}; warnings, the defects the author should fix, including exact canonical replacements for deprecated component target keys and declarations the generator dropped; and notices, advisories about a correct theme, such as a font it names but does not load. `theme.build.check` = The {check: true} receipt: theme name, an upToDate flag, the stale outputs (each {path, reason: "missing" | "outdated"}), and the full list of checked paths. Writes nothing. Resolves to null, like a normal build, when the theme produces no CSS.

`ERR_CORE_NOT_FOUND` = @astryxdesign/core/theme cannot be imported; a built, resolvable @astryxdesign/core is required
`ERR_CORE_INCOMPATIBLE` = the installed @astryxdesign/core does not export generateAdaptationCSS and the theme either declares ordered adaptations or has lineage whose adaptation use could not be observed (upgrade core)
`ERR_WRITE_FAILED` = creating the output directory or writing the outputs fails (staged temp files are rolled back)

Reads the generated module record, removes one added theme, and regenerates the whole module. The default cannot be removed until themeUse selects another added theme.

Import it from `@astryxdesign/cli/api`.

`slug` (required) = `string` = Slug of the added theme to remove.
`options.cwd` = `string` = Project directory containing the generated theme module.

`theme.app` = Every remaining theme and its imports, the default slug, the generated module path, and the remove change.

`ERR_UNKNOWN_THEME` = the theme is not added
`ERR_THEME_INVALID` = the theme is the default or generated state is invalid
`ERR_WRITE_FAILED` = the generated module cannot be written

`npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 theme remove` runs it. Read it with `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs cli/commands/theme-remove`.

## themeTargets() (theme-targets)

List every component theming target a theme can override.

Enumerates the whole themeable surface: each `defineTheme` components key, the stable class it paints, the component that declares it, and the props and states that are legal override keys under it. Same source as the Theming table `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 component <Name>` prints (the component docs), so the list cannot drift from the components, and `theme build` validates overrides against this exact set. A filter naming a component gives that component's set; anything else is a case-insensitive substring search over each target's key, class and component.

Import it from `@astryxdesign/cli/api`.

`filter` = `string` = A component name (exact, case-insensitive), or a substring of a target key, class or component. Omit for the whole surface.
`ctx.cwd` = `string` = process.cwd() = Directory the project's @astryxdesign/core is resolved from.

`theme.targets` = The echoed filter, how many components are represented, and the targets: each {key, className, component, props, states}.

`ERR_CORE_NOT_FOUND` = @astryxdesign/core cannot be resolved from cwd
`ERR_VERSIONS_UNAVAILABLE` = outside a project, or in a project with nothing installed, the Core of the release that answers is not beside it or cached, and cannot be installed into the per-user cache (offline, a registry without it, or an unwritable cache)
`ERR_UNKNOWN_COMPONENT` = a filter matches no target

`npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 theme targets` runs it. Read it with `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs cli/commands/theme-targets`.

## themeTemplate() (theme-template)

Write the annotated theme template into a project.

Writes theme.template.ts: the annotated reference for the whole theme surface, covering every defineTheme field, the token families, the component override syntax, and how a theme is consumed, with the CLI command that prints the authoritative reference for each section. Read it, copy what you need into your own theme file, delete it. Use `theme add` to use an installed built theme, extend that theme for ordinary customization, or use `theme eject` for a complete source fork. This command starts a new blank theme. Refuses to overwrite without `overwrite`, so it is safe to re-run.

Import it from `@astryxdesign/cli/api`.

`options.targetPath` = `string` = 'theme.template.ts' = Destination file. Must resolve within cwd.
`options.overwrite` = `boolean` = false = Replace an existing file instead of reporting it untouched.
`options.cwd` = `string` = process.cwd() = Directory the target path resolves against.

`theme.template` = Receipt: the path (relative to cwd), whether it was written, and the reason it was not. `exists` when a file was already there, which is a success, not a failure.

`ERR_PATH_TRAVERSAL` = the target path escapes cwd
`ERR_WRITE_FAILED` = the template file cannot be written

`npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 theme template` runs it. Read it with `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs cli/commands/theme-template`.

## upgrade() (upgrade)

After bumping @astryxdesign/core, migrate project source with codemods and update copied compositions.

Runs the codemods between `from` and the installed Core version, then refreshes the managed agent-docs block. Dry-run by default; `apply` writes changes only after the selected codemods and hooks succeed. Config codemods run before astryx.config is loaded, so they can repair an invalid config. Also updates copied compositions from their install receipts: unchanged files are updated, non-overlapping edits are merged, and conflicts are left untouched. `list` only lists codemods; `registry` only updates copied compositions. Core codemods ship inside the CLI, so a CLI older than the installed Core has none for the releases after its own version: the result then carries `cliBehindCore` with the command that runs the same upgrade on the matching CLI. In global mode: in a project, the CLI runs `upgrade` with the project's own CLI, whichever astryx command started it (in a project with no CLI of its own, the one you started); this function runs the codemods of the package it is imported from. With `cwd` outside a project, `list` lists this release's codemods, `registry` finds no copied compositions, and a migration writes nothing and fails with `ERR_VERSION_DETECT`. See `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs global` and `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs global/who-answers`.

Import it from `@astryxdesign/cli/api`.

`options.from` = `string` = Version before the dependency bump; the target is the installed @astryxdesign/core (or legacy @xds/core). Required unless `list` or `registry` is set.
`options.apply` = `boolean` = false = Write changes to disk; otherwise a dry-run preview.
`options.force` = `boolean` = false = Run codemods even when `from` is at/after the installed version.
`options.codemod` = `string` = Run only this codemod. Optional codemods run only when named here. Setting it also skips copied-composition reconciliation.
`options.skipCodemod` = `string[]` = Codemod names to exclude (e.g. to re-run past a failure).
`options.integration` = `string[]` = Explicit integration specifiers to process. Resolved beneath node_modules; absolute paths and `.` or `..` segments are rejected.
`options.path` = `string` = ./src at the project root = Source directory to scan. A path you name, in any spelling, is relative to `ctx.cwd`. When it is omitted, the upgrade scans `./src` at the project root.
`options.installDeps` = `boolean` = false = Install jscodeshift when it is missing; otherwise a missing jscodeshift throws ERR_DEP_MISSING.
`options.registry` = `boolean` = false = Only reconcile copied compositions from their install receipts; `from` is not required. Cannot be combined with `list`, `from`, `force`, `codemod`, `skipCodemod`, `integration` or `installDeps`.
`options.list` = `boolean` = false = Return the available codemods instead of running any.
`ctx.cwd` = `string` = process.cwd() = Any folder in the project to upgrade. The upgrade runs at the project root: the nearest folder at or above it whose package.json declares an Astryx package, or that a workspace whose root declares one lists, found without passing a repository root or counting the home folder. With no such folder, it runs in `ctx.cwd`. File paths in the result are relative to `ctx.cwd`, except that a run at the project root names copied-composition paths relative to the scanned source directory.

`upgrade.list` = Every available codemod, oldest→newest, as {name, title, version, optional}, returned when `list` is set; nothing is run.
`upgrade.registry` = A dry-run or apply receipt for copied compositions, including safe updates, clean merges, conflicts, missing files, and invalid receipts.
`upgrade.status` = A short-circuit outcome (no codemods executed): `up_to_date` (`from` is at/after the installed target and no `force`), `no_codemods` (none apply to the range), or `config_fixable` (dry-run preview that a pending config codemod would repair an invalid astryx.config). up_to_date and no_codemods carry the agent-docs summary and, when receipts are found, the copied-composition summary; config_fixable carries configError, configCodemods, suggestedCommand, message, note, and the agent-docs summary. When the installed Core is newer than the CLI, no_codemods and config_fixable also carry cliBehindCore ({cliVersion, command}): this CLI has no codemods for the releases after cliVersion, and command runs the same upgrade with the CLI release that matches the installed Core.
`upgrade.run` = The terminal run receipt: from, to, codemods (count), integrations, agentDocs, agentDocsRefreshed, registryCompositions (when receipts are found), sourcePathFound (false when the resolved `path` does not exist, so nothing was scanned), filesChanged, transformsApplied, modifiedFiles, protectedFiles, declinedCandidates (left unchanged for manual review, including code a codemod identified but cannot migrate; never incomplete), regenerate (generated files to rebuild, with their commands), errors, and complete. When a protected file still requires a change, including a protected file in regenerate, complete is false and errorCode is ERR_CODEMOD_PROTECTED; the CLI exits nonzero while preserving the structured receipt. A run that fails after its codemods ran throws instead (see throws), and the thrown AstryxError carries the same receipt on `receipt`, with complete false and errorCode set to its code. A file in regenerate that nothing protects is such a failure: it is also in errors, and the run throws ERR_CODEMOD_FAILED. When the installed Core is newer than the CLI, it also carries cliBehindCore ({cliVersion, command}): codemods for the releases after cliVersion did not run, and command runs the same upgrade with the matching CLI.

`ERR_INVALID_ARGUMENT` = `from` is missing (and neither `list` nor `registry` is set); `list` and `registry` are both set; `list` is combined with `from`, `force`, `apply`, `path` (non-default), `codemod`, `skipCodemod`, `integration` or `installDeps`; `registry` is combined with `from`, `force`, `codemod`, `skipCodemod`, `integration` or `installDeps`; an `integration` specifier is invalid or not installed; or astryx.config fails to load or validate and no pending config codemod repairs it (when core codemods already wrote files, the error carries their receipt on `receipt`)
`ERR_INVALID_VERSION` = `from` is not a valid semver string
`ERR_PATH_TRAVERSAL` = `path` resolves outside the project root
`ERR_VERSION_DETECT` = the project has installed neither @astryxdesign/core nor legacy @xds/core in its own node_modules, nor, for a member its workspace lists, in a folder up to the workspace root (with no Astryx project, in `ctx.cwd`'s own node_modules); with `registry`, only when copied-composition receipts exist and @astryxdesign/core is not installed
`ERR_DEP_MISSING` = jscodeshift is missing and `installDeps` is not set, or installing it failed
`ERR_UNKNOWN_CODEMOD` = the version range has codemods but none remain selected: `codemod` names no codemod in the range, or `skipCodemod` excludes all of them
`ERR_CODEMOD_FAILED` = one or more codemods failed (including a generated file to regenerate that nothing protects), or a post-codemod hook failed, and no protected file still needs a change (otherwise an upgrade.run receipt with complete: false is returned). The error carries the run's receipt on `receipt`: the files already changed, each failure in errors, complete: false
`ERR_CODEMOD_PROTECTION_SOURCE` = a working-tree protection declaration cannot be read or parsed before writes begin, or after post-codemod hooks rewrite it (the error then carries the receipt on `receipt`)

`npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 upgrade` runs it. Read it with `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs cli/commands/upgrade`.

## validateIntegration() (validate-integration)

Validate a single Astryx integration package and report its issues.

Validates exactly ONE integration at a time: the local package rooted at cwd (no `pkg`), or an installed package resolved from cwd/node_modules (`pkg` given). It loads and schema-checks the manifest, verifies each declared contribution root exists, and runs the codemod/template/component/docs/theme validators, returning every finding as an AstryxIntegrationIssue. A missing local manifest is guidance (name null, no issues), not an error, so callers can stay exit-0 in a non-integration directory. It also checks every doc the package ships under its roots (component, template, docs topic, theme, and translation, served or not) against the published authoring type for its kind, as `tsc` would, with the project's own `typescript` (or, where `typescript` is missing or has no JavaScript compiler API, as TypeScript 7 does, the `@typescript/typescript6` it installs): an unknown field, a missing required field, or a value outside a field's type is a warning in `docTypes` naming the field and a fix. A test fixture under `__tests__` in the components or docs root is counted, not checked. Without TypeScript, `docTypes` is `skipped` with a reason.

Import it from `@astryxdesign/cli/api`.

`pkg` = `string` = Installed package name to validate; omit to validate the package rooted at cwd.
`options.cwd` = `string` = Directory to resolve the local package / node_modules from.

`integration.validate` = The result envelope: `data.validated`, false when nothing was validated — with no `package.json` at all, `data.issues` carries one `no_package` error-severity issue so the command exits 1; with a `package.json` but no integration manifest, `data.issues` is empty, which means "not looked at", not "healthy"; `data.name` and `data.version` of the validated package (both null when `data.validated` is false; `data.name` is `(local package)` when the local package.json has no readable name), plus `data.issues`, an AstryxIntegrationIssue[] of {code, severity: `warning` | `error`, message, fix?, file?, line?}: `fix` is the change that resolves the issue, and `file` and `line` where it is, relative to the package, when the check knows them; and `data.notes` when there are any: {code, message, next?} information beside the issues; a note fails nothing by default, and one with `next: true` counts as a warning under `integration check --next`, fails `integration check --strict --next`, and fails `--strict` from the next minor release. Notes include `invalid_cli_command` for a `cliCommand` that was ignored as malformed and `cli_peer_version` when the running CLI is outside the `@astryxdesign/cli` peer range of the package, and the package layout findings added after the last minor release, each with its fix in the message: `duplicate_component_doc`, `symlinked_root`, `unreadable_file`, `invalid_package_json` (no `name` or `version`), `no_provider_id`, and `source_without_component_doc` for a doc whose file name differs from its source only in letter case where the two still pair; and `doc_name_mismatch` and `unknown_block_component` (see `docNames` and `blockComponents`); they become warnings in the next minor release. For the commands a topic writes, `runner_command` (written with a package runner), `plain_command` (written bare), `package_manager_command` (written for one package manager) and `doc_token` (a token that does not parse) notes each give the file, line and the token to write. A `doc_target_not_found` note names a doc whose `replaces` or `extends` names no topic and no guide of the CLI's docs or the package's own (such as a namespace, with the guides below it), so it changes nothing unless an app also installs a package that provides it, and a `doc_section_unplaced` note a section whose `before` or `after` names no section of the topic or guide it extends, so it is added at the end, and a `duplicate_guide_replacement` note two docs of the package that replace one guide, of which only the last is read; they become warnings in the next minor release. When the manifest loads, `data.docTypes` holds the doc type check: `status` (`checked` | `skipped`), `reason` when skipped, `typescript`, `docs` (doc values checked), `findings` ({doc, line, export, type, field, problem: `unknown_field` | `missing_field` | `wrong_type`, severity: `warning`, message, fix}), `unchecked` ({doc, reason}: a doc that could not be fully checked, or a root its reader cannot read), and `fixtures` when the components or docs root holds test fixture docs under `__tests__`: how many, none of them checked. When the manifest loads, `data.docNames` lists the component doc names it could not judge: `status` (`checked`), `findings` (always empty; a doc name the module its import names provably does not export is a `doc_name_mismatch` note, with its fix in the message) and `unchecked` ({file, name, reason}: a doc whose `name` differs from the name it is listed under and whose source exports cannot all be read, such as a re-export from another package). When the manifest loads, `data.blockComponents` lists the component names templates give in `exampleFor` or `componentsUsed` that could not be judged: `status` (`checked`), `findings` (always empty; a name neither the package nor Core has, and the template does not import, is an `unknown_block_component` note, with its fix in the message) and `unchecked` ({file, name, reason}: a name the template may reach through anything other than named imports and re-exports from Core, React, StyleX, local helpers or the entry of the package itself, such as an import from another package, a default or namespace import, an alias of or member read off an imported binding, require() or a dynamic import(), or a local module that cannot be read, or any name Core would have to resolve when Core is not installed). Since 0.7.3 each import apps cannot use is a note in `data.notes`, its fix inside the message, listed only: it does not fail this command or `integration check --strict`, and fails `--strict` from the next minor release. The codes are `component_import_not_exported`, `component_import_other_package`, `component_import_missing_name`, `example_import_not_exported`, `example_import_missing_name`, `template_import_not_exported`, `template_import_outside_root`, `template_private_import`, `template_import_missing_name` and `template_no_default_export`. Since 0.7.4 the examples a package ships are checked the same way: `component_without_example` (a published component no block template shows with `exampleFor` and `isShowcase: true`, or names in `alsoShowcaseFor`), `template_category` (a template category written as a path, such as `components/X`), `showcase_not_standalone` (a showcase that imports server-only code or reads `process.env` past `NODE_ENV`) and `template_asset_not_packed` (a `new URL(…, import.meta.url)` asset that is missing, or that `npm pack --dry-run` leaves out of the package). When npm cannot list the package's files, an asset no `files` entry can reach is still a note, and any other is listed in `data.exampleAssets` (`{status: 'checked', findings: [], unchecked}`, present only when it lists any) as {file, asset, reason}; `integration check` counts them as not compared. When the manifest loads, `data.publicImports` is `{status: 'checked', findings: [], unchecked}`: `unchecked` lists each import the check could not judge, as {file, specifier, reason}, the reason starting `example <label>:` for an import in a component example: an `exports` target not built yet; a module whose export list cannot be read in full (CommonJS, or a declaration file it cannot read); a root import in a package with no `exports` (the root module `main` names is not read); every name an import (other than a component doc's own component) names that its module does not export, while a TypeScript file in the package has a `declare module` block for a relative path or the package's own name or a subpath of it, which can add names to that module (a `declare module` in a comment, `declare global`, a wildcard such as `'*.css'`, and another package's name do not count; a file whose text has `declare module` but that cannot be parsed counts); the same for every such name when the package has more than 5,000 files to search for that block; a deep path into build output not built yet in a package with no `exports`; a template import of Core when `@astryxdesign/core` is not installed beside the package (a `packages/core` of the workspace under another name does not count); every import of the package's own name when package.json has no `name` or a `name` that is not a bare package name; one entry for the whole check when package.json cannot be read; and an import of a subpath whose `exports` entry has only a `types` target, unless it is `import type`, every binding is an inline `type`, or every name it imports is a type its types file declares: a value import of a name that file does not declare as a type, a namespace or side-effect import, or any import when the types file cannot be read (it may be build output). `integration check` counts the unchecked as not compared; they never fail it. `data.olderCliNotes` ({file, kind: `template` | `namespace`, field, message}), for the local package, lists each descriptor field a release before 0.7.4 refuses while the package's CLI peer range admits one, such as `stability` on a template or namespace doc; it is present only when it has entries, is never counted, and never fails a check.
